original_value: In this paper, a novel Pixel-Voxel network is proposed for dense 3D semantic mapping, which can perform dense 3D mapping while simultaneously recognizing and labelling the semantic category each point in the 3D map. In our approach, we fully leverage the advantages of different modalities. That is, the PixelNet can learn the high-level contextual information from 2D RGB images, and the VoxelNet can learn 3D geometrical shapes from the 3D point cloud. Unlike the existing architecture that fuses score maps from different modalities with equal weights, we propose a softmax weighted fusion stack that adaptively learns the varying contributions of PixelNet and VoxelNet and fuses the score maps according to their respective confidence levels. Our approach achieved competitive results on both the SUN RGB-D and NYU V2 benchmarks, while the runtime of the proposed system is boosted to around 13 Hz, enabling near-real-time performance using an i7 eight-cores PC with a single Titan X GPU.

result.paraphrase: The paper proposes a new Pixel-Voxel network for dense 3D semantic mapping, capable of producing dense 3D maps while also identifying and labeling the semantic class of each point in the map. The method fully exploits the strengths of different modalities: PixelNet learns high-level contextual information from 2D RGB images, while VoxelNet learns 3D geometric shapes from the 3D point cloud. Rather than combining score maps from multiple modalities with equal weights as in prior architectures, it introduces a softmax-weighted fusion stack that adaptively learns the relative contributions of PixelNet and VoxelNet and merges the score maps according to their confidence levels. The approach achieves competitive results on both the SUN RGB-D and NYU V2 benchmarks, and the system runs at about 13 Hz, providing near-real-time performance on an i7 eight-core PC with a single Titan X GPU.
